prediction_text: Canterbury (Archbishop Laud) will die a violent death by beheading — his head struck off by a sharp weapon (sword/axe) in execution, not a natural death in prison. Mars in an airy, humane sign disposes the manner: death by the blade, publicly inflicted.
timing: Month scale: the Moon wants seven degrees of the body of Mars and applies through the Sun near the 8th cusp — the fatal perfection falls within months (the seven degrees read as the term to the execution), while he remains a prisoner.
basis: Lilly: for a churchman the 9th house cusp is taken as his Ascendant; Saturn, lord of that sign, is in his fall, long retrograde, and posited in the 12th — the fallen, imprisoned, helpless state of the quesited. The Moon separates from Saturn and applies to the Sun near the cusp of the 8th (house of death); the Sun in a fiery sign applies to an opposition of Mars, the dispositor of the aged Bishop; Mars in an airy and humane sign signifies a violent death by a sharp weapon upon the body of a man — beheading — and the Moon wanting seven degrees of Mars's body times it. No testimony of natural death or release intervenes.
